target_customer: Grocery and convenience retailers wanting checkout-free stores, later retail operators buying vision analytics
problem: Shoppers wait in checkout lines and retailers lack Amazon Go style technology; Standard retrofitted stores with camera-only computer vision so shoppers could just walk out.
business_model: B2B enterprise software and hardware deployments to retailers
product_category: Retail computer vision, autonomous checkout and analytics

founders.name: Jordan Fisher
founders.background_notes: Became board chairman in 2024 when COO Angie Westbrock became CEO.

competitors.name: Zippin
competitors.what: Cashierless store using shelf sensors plus cameras
competitors.traction_then: Opened a prototype store in San Francisco in August 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Tracking many shoppers and product interactions with cameras only, in real stores, was research-grade computer vision in 2017 and also needed custom hardware.

defensibility.rationale: Hard vision stack and retrofit approach (no turnstiles or shelf sensors) were difficult to copy, but costs and long retailer pilots limited lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon Go was already operating pilots and opened to the public in 2018; Amazon did not buy Standard. A vendor table claims Amazon later closed Go stores, which is unverified.

market_need_then: Amazon Go's 2016 announcement validated demand for checkout-free retail and pushed retailers to look for a vendor alternative.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in retail tech press as an Amazon Go rival, but the generic name is shared with other companies and no brand assets or community were found.

pivots.why: Company announced a VISION analytics product in March 2024; one low authority site says it moved away from autonomous checkout (unverified).

outcome_analysis: Standard raised a reported $150M Series C at about $1B in February 2021 on camera-only autonomous checkout, a hard technical problem with Amazon Go creating demand. It remains active with a smaller team and, in 2024, a new CEO and a pivot toward retail vision analytics, which suggests checkout alone did not scale as hoped, but no source states why.
notes: Unverified, from aggregators with conflicting leads: Series A $40M in 2018-11 led by Initialized Capital; Series B $35M in 2019-07 at a $535M post-money; total raised about $231M to $239M. The company site fetch returned empty content. Series C lead conflicts between SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and SB Investment Advisers. The only dated competitor source is 2019; Amazon Go (announced December 2016) is a larger incumbent and not listed as a competitor entry for lack of a dated source near the batch. The name was Standard Cognition at founding; timing of the rebrand to Standard AI is unknown. TrueUp lists 60 employees versus 150 on YC, unreconciled.
